newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MIDF says not selling Oriental Bank.
newsitem.headline: MIDF says not selling Oriental Bank.

text.p: Malaysian Industrial Development Finance Bhd (MIDF) said on Friday it does not intend to sell its stake in Oriental Bank Bhd.
In a one-paragraph statement to the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange, MIDF said it "does not intend to dispose of its equity interest in Oriental Bank Bhd".
Malaysia's largest conglomerate Sime Darby Bhd had announced in December it had approval from the central bank to start negotiating with MIDF to buy a 51 percent stake in Oriental.
MIDF owns a 78.4 percent equity in medium-sized Oriental, which had 41 branches as at March 31, 1996.
Sime had planned to merge Oriental with its Sime Bank Bhd, which late last year changed its name from United Malayan Banking Bhd.
Sime officials could not be reached for comment on MIDF's decision.
Sime Darby's group chief executive Nik Mohamed Yaacob said in mid-December that financial services would be the "prime core activity" of the company in the future.
In September last year, MIDF received approval from the central bank to list the stock of Oriental.
